title: Religion, Politics and Public Life
welcome_lead: From the Vatican to the Iranian Revolution — explore how religion shapes politics, and vice versa.
meta_desc: IBDP Religious Studies Adventure: religion and politics across regimes and cases.
final_note: You have studied religion's many political faces. Disentangling them illuminates contemporary affairs.

concepts.def: Form of government in which religious leaders rule in the name of divine authority, e.g. Iran post-1979.
French principle of strict separation of state and religion in public life.
Robert Bellah's concept of national religiosity surrounding the symbols of a state.
Reflection on the relation between religious doctrine and political life.
Movements fusing religious identity with political nationalism, e.g. Hindu nationalism in India.
Latin American theological movement (1960s-) emphasising God's preferential option for the poor.

walkthroughs.body_html: State-religion relations range from established churches (Church of England) and concordats (Vatican-Italy 1929) to strict separation (US First Amendment, French laïcité of 1905). Each carries different costs and benefits for religious freedom and public life.

The Iranian Revolution (1979) installed a Shia theocracy. The US religious right shaped policy on abortion, education and bioethics. Liberation theology animated Latin American activism. Hindu nationalism (BJP, RSS) reshapes Indian politics; Buddhist nationalism in Myanmar and Sri Lanka also raises ethical concerns.

Bellah's 'civil religion' framework helps interpret American presidential rhetoric, oaths and ceremonies. Interfaith initiatives such as the Parliament of the World's Religions and the United Religions Initiative encourage dialogue. The 'post-secular' (Habermas) recognises religion's continuing public role.
